title: Stories of the Unseen: Angels, Books, and Messengers
summary:
Has your 7-9 year old ever asked you to tell them a story about something they can't see? Perhaps about jinn, or about Paradise and Hellfire? At this age, children's imaginations expand, and they become ready to receive deeper concepts about the world around them, including the unseen realms that we don't perceive with our eyes. This is a wonderful opportunity to instill faith in what Allah and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, have informed us, so we believe and affirm it.

Belief in angels, books, and messengers is a fundamental pillar of our creed, and it gives children a sense of connection to a wider, more sacred world. Angels are noble, luminous creations whom Allah created to obey Him; among them is Jibreel, who brought down revelation, and among them are those who protect us, and among them are the two scribes who record our deeds. The books are guidance and light sent down by Allah for people; the greatest and most complete of them is the Noble Qur'an, the word of Allah, which He has guaranteed to preserve. As for the messengers, they are prophets sent by Allah to teach people their religion; the first of them was Nuh and the last was Muhammad ﷺ. These pillars are not just theoretical information; rather, they are concepts that influence a child's daily behavior and actions.

To make these concepts alive in our children's lives, we can connect them to their daily behavior. When a child knows that there is an angel recording their deeds, they will be keen to ensure they dictate good, and they will feel a greater responsibility for their actions. And when they love the Qur'an because it is the word of their Lord, they will learn it and be keen to recite it and reflect upon it. This is an opportunity to instill reverence and love for these great pillars in a warm and accessible way, far from burdensome obligation, so that love and firm faith may grow in their hearts.
try_this: Tonight: Before bed, tell your child a short story about an angel or a messenger, or listen together to a short verse from the Noble Qur'an and discuss it in simple language.
reflection_prompts: How can I make belief in the unseen a natural and beloved part of my child's daily life without them feeling fear or burden?
What are the best ways to foster my child's love for the Noble Qur'an and make it part of their routine without it becoming a heavy obligation?
parent_script: “Imagine there's a noble angel writing down all your good deeds today. What would you like to fill your scroll with?”
assistant_prompts: How do I explain to my 7-9 year old who angels are and what their functions are in a simple, age-appropriate way?
